questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: A consumer calls an MLO to ask about general rate ranges and requests product information. The consumer has not yet provided the items needed to constitute an application. Under Regulation Z, this contact is best classified as:

answers.text: An application that triggers the 3-business-day Loan Estimate clock
A pre-application inquiry that does not yet trigger the Loan Estimate clock
A formal request for a Closing Disclosure
A request for a Verification of Deposit

explanations.a: Wrong — without the six items defined as an application, the LE clock has not started.
explanations.b: Correct — until the consumer provides all six application items, the contact is a pre-application inquiry under 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(3).
explanations.c: Wrong — a CD is not requested until much later in the loan cycle.
explanations.d: Wrong — a VOD is an asset-verification document, not a disclosure trigger.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: During an initial inquiry, an MLO may ask the consumer general questions about products and rates without triggering an application. The MLO should avoid requesting any of the six items that would convert the contact into an application. Which question would NOT, by itself, contribute to making the contact an application?

answers.text: What loan products are you most interested in hearing about?
What is your full legal name?
What is your Social Security number?
What is the property address?

explanations.a: Correct — asking about product preferences does not capture any of the six application items under 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(3).
explanations.b: Wrong — name is one of the six items.
explanations.c: Wrong — SSN is one of the six items.
explanations.d: Wrong — property address is one of the six items.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: On a residential mortgage application, the borrower is using a gift to fund part of the down payment. The lender must document the gift and verify acceptable donor status. A gift donor on a conventional residential loan must generally:

answers.text: Be a creditor or financial institution making a loan
Be an unrelated individual to ensure independence
Provide collateral equal to the gift amount
Have a documented qualifying relationship to the borrower (such as a relative, fiance, or domestic partner) and provide a signed gift letter stating the funds need not be repaid

explanations.a: Wrong — the donor cannot be a creditor giving a loan, since gifts must not be repayable.
explanations.b: Wrong — agency rules generally require a relationship; an unrelated third party is typically not eligible.
explanations.c: Wrong — collateral is not part of a gift; gifts are not loans.
explanations.d: Correct — Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac selling guides require an eligible donor relationship and a gift letter affirming the funds are not a loan.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Before the consumer indicates intent to proceed, Regulation Z restricts what fees a creditor can charge. The rule preserves the consumer's right to shop without pressure. Before the consumer's indication of intent to proceed, the creditor may charge only:

answers.text: An origination fee equal to 1% of the loan amount
Discount points selected by the consumer
A bona fide and reasonable fee for obtaining a credit report
An appraisal deposit equal to the estimated appraisal cost

explanations.a: Wrong — origination fees cannot be collected pre-intent.
explanations.b: Wrong — discount-point fees cannot be collected before intent to proceed.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(2)(i)(B) allows only a bona fide and reasonable credit-report fee before intent to proceed.
explanations.d: Wrong — appraisal deposits cannot be collected before intent to proceed.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: MLOs handle nonpublic personal information from consumers. Mishandling this information can violate GLBA and state law. An MLO who collects a consumer's Social Security number, income documents, and bank statements must:

answers.text: Safeguard the information consistent with the company's GLBA-required information security program
Post the information to a public website for transparency
Forward the information to any party requesting it
Discard the information immediately after the call to avoid compliance risk

explanations.a: Correct — GLBA's Safeguards Rule (16 CFR 314) requires an information security program protecting nonpublic personal information.
explanations.b: Wrong — public posting violates GLBA and state privacy law.
explanations.c: Wrong — disclosure to unauthorized parties violates GLBA's privacy rule.
explanations.d: Wrong — record retention obligations under TILA, RESPA, and HMDA preclude immediate destruction.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: At application, the consumer receives certain initial disclosures along with the Loan Estimate. Both Regulation Z and Regulation X drive the timing. Which disclosure is generally required within 3 business days of application along with the Loan Estimate on a purchase transaction?

answers.text: The final Closing Disclosure for the transaction
The Servicing Transfer Disclosure issued at servicing transfer
The CFPB special information booklet (Your Home Loan Toolkit)
An IRS Form 4506-C tax transcript request

explanations.a: Wrong — the CD is delivered later in the process, not at application.
explanations.b: Wrong — the Servicing Transfer Disclosure is issued at transfer, not at application.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(g) requires the special information booklet within 3 business days of application on purchase loans.
explanations.d: Wrong — the 4506-C is a verification document, not an application-stage consumer disclosure.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The application file includes the items needed to evaluate creditworthiness and to issue accurate disclosures. The MLO should explain each form to the consumer. A standard residential mortgage application form widely used in the industry is:

answers.text: The HUD-1 Settlement Statement
The Uniform Residential Loan Application (Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac Form 1003)
The IRS Form 1040
The Closing Disclosure form

explanations.a: Wrong — the HUD-1 was a settlement statement, replaced by the CD under TRID.
explanations.b: Correct — Form 1003 (URLA) is the industry-standard residential mortgage application.
explanations.c: Wrong — Form 1040 is a tax return, not a loan application.
explanations.d: Wrong — the CD is a closing disclosure, not an application form.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Regulation B permits creditors to ask certain questions on residential mortgage applications that would otherwise touch protected bases. The exceptions support fair-lending oversight and underwriting. On a residential mortgage application, an MLO MAY ask:

answers.text: The applicant's plans for childbearing
Whether the applicant practices a particular religion
The applicant's political party affiliation
Whether income from alimony, child support, or separate maintenance should be considered, with notice that disclosure is optional

explanations.a: Wrong — childbearing inquiries are barred by 12 CFR 1002.5(d).
explanations.b: Wrong — religion is a prohibited basis under ECOA.
explanations.c: Wrong — political affiliation has no bearing on creditworthiness and is irrelevant.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.5(c)(2) permits asking, with notice that disclosure is optional unless the applicant wants the income considered.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: After receiving an application, the MLO must provide certain disclosures to the borrower. The communication preserves the integrity of the disclosure timing rules. If the LE was placed in the mail, the consumer is presumed to have received it:

answers.text: On the same day it was mailed
On the next business day after mailing
On the second business day after mailing
On the third business day after the LE was placed in the mail

explanations.a: Wrong — the regulation provides a 3-business-day mailing presumption, not same-day.
explanations.b: Wrong — next-business-day is shorter than the regulatory presumption.
explanations.c: Wrong — second-business-day is shorter than the regulatory presumption.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(1)(iv) presumes receipt 3 business days after mailing.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: An MLO and consumer have been discussing options. Once the MLO has all six items defined as an application, the MLO cannot delay the LE by withholding action. The consumer 'completes the application' as soon as the MLO has received:

answers.text: Verified asset and income documents and employment verifications
Name, monthly income, Social Security number, property address, estimated property value, and the loan amount sought
A signed and notarized loan agreement and title report
The full underwriting package, including appraisal and title commitment

explanations.a: Wrong — verification documents are not part of the application definition under TRID.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(3) defines application as receipt of these six items.
explanations.c: Wrong — the loan agreement is signed at consummation, not at application.
explanations.d: Wrong — underwriting documents follow application; they do not define it.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: To pull a credit report and verify employment, the lender needs the consumer's authorization. The authorization documents permissible purpose for FCRA. An MLO obtains a credit report only after:

answers.text: Obtaining the consumer's authorization in a manner sufficient to establish a permissible purpose under FCRA
Issuing the Closing Disclosure to the consumer
Submitting the application to underwriting for approval
The consumer signs the final note and security instrument

explanations.a: Correct — 15 USC 1681b(a)(2)-(3) require either consumer instruction or a permissible purpose, typically documented by an authorization in mortgage transactions.
explanations.b: Wrong — credit pulls happen at application, long before the CD.
explanations.c: Wrong — pulls precede underwriting, not the reverse.
explanations.d: Wrong — pulls precede consummation by weeks, not after.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: During asset verification, an underwriter notices a large, recent deposit on the borrower's bank statement that is not consistent with payroll history. The deposit must be addressed for asset qualification. A 'large deposit' on a bank statement that is unsourced typically:

answers.text: Increases the borrower's qualifying income amount
May be subtracted only from the seller's net proceeds at closing
Must be sourced and documented by the borrower or excluded from qualifying assets
Becomes part of the down payment automatically without sourcing

explanations.a: Wrong — deposits affect assets, not income.
explanations.b: Wrong — bank deposits do not net against seller proceeds.
explanations.c: Correct — agency guides require sourcing of large deposits relative to monthly income; unsourced funds are excluded from qualifying.
explanations.d: Wrong — automatic inclusion as down payment without sourcing violates agency standards.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Employment verification is a standard step in residential mortgage underwriting. The verification confirms the income used in qualifying. A typical written verification of employment (VOE) is sent:

answers.text: To the borrower for self-completion and return to the lender
Directly from the lender to the employer for the employer to complete and return
To the credit bureau for confirmation of work history
To the IRS for confirmation of W-2 reporting

explanations.a: Wrong — borrower self-completion would defeat the verification.
explanations.b: Correct — VOEs are sent directly to the employer to maintain independence of the verification.
explanations.c: Wrong — credit bureaus do not verify employment.
explanations.d: Wrong — the IRS does not provide written employment verifications.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Lenders use the IRS to validate income reported on a loan application by requesting copies of filed tax returns or transcripts. The borrower must consent. A signed Form 4506-T or 4506-C authorizes:

answers.text: The IRS to amend the borrower's prior tax returns
The credit bureau to send a tri-merge report to the lender
Notarization of income figures on the application
Release of the borrower's tax return transcripts to the lender or designee

explanations.a: Wrong — these forms do not authorize amendments to returns.
explanations.b: Wrong — credit reports come from authorized credit pulls, not from 4506-T/C.
explanations.c: Wrong — these forms do not provide notarization.
explanations.d: Correct — Form 4506-T/4506-C authorizes the IRS to release transcripts to the lender or designee.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: To document liquid funds available for the down payment, lenders typically request bank statements or a verification of deposit. The procedure documents asset reserves. A Verification of Deposit (VOD) is sent:

answers.text: To the borrower's depository institution to verify the balance and average balance of named accounts
To the IRS to confirm filed tax returns and adjusted gross income
To the local recorder of deeds to confirm property liens
To the title agent to confirm escrowed funds at the title company

explanations.a: Correct — VODs are sent to the depository institution to verify account balances independent of the borrower.
explanations.b: Wrong — the IRS does not verify deposits.
explanations.c: Wrong — recorders do not verify deposits.
explanations.d: Wrong — title agents do not verify borrower bank balances.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: An MLO matching a borrower with a loan must consider the borrower's circumstances and financial profile. The match supports compliance with Regulation Z's loan originator rules and CFPB guidance. Selecting a product is most consistent with the suitability standard when the MLO:

answers.text: Recommends the product that pays the MLO the highest commission
Picks the loan with the lowest rate, regardless of borrower fit
Recommends a product whose features fit the borrower's documented needs, finances, and goals
Defers entirely to the borrower's stated preferences without explanation

explanations.a: Wrong — compensation-driven recommendations violate the LO compensation rule under 12 CFR 1026.36(d).
explanations.b: Wrong — lowest rate alone does not establish fit; product features and risk profile matter.
explanations.c: Correct — fit between the consumer's needs/goals and the product features is the suitability standard.
explanations.d: Wrong — the MLO's professional duty is to inform; pure deference without explanation does not satisfy suitability.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: On a residential mortgage application, the loan type field must reflect the actual loan being applied for. Misrepresenting the type can violate Reg N and program guidelines. If a borrower is applying for an FHA-insured loan, the application:

answers.text: Should be marked as conventional to expand eligibility options
Should be marked as VA to obtain better terms for the borrower
Must be marked as FHA so disclosures and program rules align with the loan type
Should be left blank until underwriting decides on a loan type

explanations.a: Wrong — misclassifying as conventional misaligns disclosures and program rules.
explanations.b: Wrong — misclassifying as VA when the borrower is not eligible misrepresents the loan and would mislead investors.
explanations.c: Correct — accurate loan-type identification ensures proper disclosures and program compliance.
explanations.d: Wrong — leaving the field blank does not satisfy the application requirements; the loan type is established by program eligibility, not underwriting choice.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Regulation Z's anti-steering rule restricts when a loan originator may direct a borrower to a particular loan. Presenting a meaningful menu helps satisfy the anti-steering safe harbor. Under the anti-steering safe harbor, the originator presents the consumer with loan options that include:

answers.text: Only the loan with the lowest stated rate available in the market

The loan with the lowest interest rate, the loan with the lowest origination/discount points and lender credits, and the loan with the lowest rate without certain risky features (such as negative amortization or prepayment penalty)
Only loans the originator's company offers exclusively
Two loans with similar terms and one option clearly marked as best

explanations.a: Wrong — a single option does not satisfy the safe harbor's choice requirement.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.36(e) defines the safe-harbor menu by these three loan options.
explanations.c: Wrong — limiting to one company's products fails the anti-steering rule's purpose.
explanations.d: Wrong — pre-selecting a 'best' option for the consumer is the steering the rule prohibits.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The zero-tolerance category covers fees the consumer cannot shop for and certain fees paid to specified parties. Going over by a single dollar is a violation absent a valid changed circumstance. Which of the following is in the zero-tolerance category?

answers.text: Charges paid to the mortgage broker or to an affiliate of the broker
An owner's title insurance policy purchased at the consumer's option
Daily prepaid interest collected at closing
Hazard insurance premiums for a policy chosen by the consumer

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(i) places fees paid to the broker or its affiliates in the zero-tolerance bucket.
explanations.b: Wrong — owner's title insurance purchased at borrower option is unlimited variance, not zero tolerance.
explanations.c: Wrong — per-diem prepaid interest is unlimited variance.
explanations.d: Wrong — hazard insurance is unlimited variance.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The 10% tolerance bucket addresses situations where the consumer can shop for a service but selects a provider from the creditor's written list. Charges in this bucket are aggregated, not measured individually. The 10% tolerance limit applies when:

answers.text: Lender origination fees increase between LE and CD
The borrower changes the property at the last minute
Recording fees decrease between LE and CD
The aggregate of recording fees and charges for third-party services consumer-shopped from the creditor's written list increases by more than 10% over the disclosed total

explanations.a: Wrong — lender origination fees are zero-tolerance.
explanations.b: Wrong — a property change is a changed circumstance, not a tolerance bucket itself.
explanations.c: Wrong — decreases do not violate tolerance rules.
explanations.d: Correct — the 10% test is applied in aggregate to the recording fees and shopped-on-list services bucket under 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(ii).

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Some charges fall into an unlimited-variance category because they are outside the lender's reasonable control or the consumer chose the provider off-list. These charges may differ at closing without a tolerance violation. Which of the following is in the unlimited-variance category?

answers.text: Property taxes paid to the local taxing authority
Lender origination charges disclosed on the LE
Transfer taxes paid to a state or local government
Title insurance fees from a creditor-affiliated title agent

explanations.a: Correct — property taxes are set by the taxing authority and fall in the unlimited variance bucket per 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(iii).
explanations.b: Wrong — lender origination charges are zero-tolerance.
explanations.c: Wrong — transfer taxes are zero-tolerance.
explanations.d: Wrong — affiliated title charges are zero-tolerance.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: When a creditor's actual charges exceed the disclosed amount beyond permitted tolerances, Regulation Z requires correction. The cure preserves the consumer's right to the disclosed pricing. A tolerance violation occurs when:

answers.text: The consumer pays exactly the disclosed amount at closing
Property taxes increase between the LE and the closing date
The consumer voluntarily selects a costlier title provider off the creditor's list
A zero-tolerance fee at closing exceeds the LE amount, or a 10%-bucket aggregate increases by more than 10%, without a valid changed circumstance

explanations.a: Wrong — charging the disclosed amount is compliant.
explanations.b: Wrong — property taxes are unlimited variance and changes do not violate tolerances.
explanations.c: Wrong — off-list shopping shifts charges to unlimited variance, not a violation.
explanations.d: Correct — these are the two violation patterns under 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3).

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Charges before the consumer indicates intent to proceed are limited. The narrow exception preserves the LE shopping period. The fee that may be collected before intent to proceed must be:

answers.text: Equal to 1% of the loan amount
Disclosed only on the CD
Bona fide and reasonable in amount, and limited to obtaining the consumer's credit report
Refundable only if the loan does not close

explanations.a: Wrong — there is no 1% allowance pre-intent.
explanations.b: Wrong — the LE, not the CD, governs disclosure.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(2)(i)(B) limits pre-intent collection to a bona fide and reasonable credit report fee.
explanations.d: Wrong — the regulation does not define this fee by refundability.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: A revised LE may be issued only after a defined trigger, called a 'changed circumstance.' The trigger may reset tolerance baselines for affected charges. Which of the following is a changed circumstance under Regulation Z?

answers.text: The consumer changes their mind about the closing date
An extraordinary event beyond the parties' control, new and material consumer-provided information, or new transaction-specific information the creditor relied on for an estimate
The lender wants to increase its origination fee
The MLO's commission goal for the month has not yet been met

explanations.a: Wrong — closing date changes alone are not changed circumstances.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(iv) defines the three categories of changed circumstance.
explanations.c: Wrong — lender preference for higher fees is not a changed circumstance.
explanations.d: Wrong — internal sales targets are irrelevant to changed-circumstance status.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: After application, the creditor must inform the consumer of certain rights and procedures. One key disclosure addresses how appraisal information will be handled. On a residential mortgage application secured by a first lien on a 1-4 family dwelling, the creditor must inform the borrower:

answers.text: Of the borrower's right to a free copy of the property survey
That the application requires notarization to be valid
That the application is irrevocable once signed
Of the right to receive a free copy of any appraisal or other written valuation, no later than 3 business days after application

explanations.a: Wrong — there is no federal right-to-survey notice at application.
explanations.b: Wrong — applications do not require notarization.
explanations.c: Wrong — applications are not legally irrevocable upon signing.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.14(a)(2) requires the appraisal-copy notice within 3 business days of application.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: When a referring party has an ownership interest in a settlement service provider, RESPA requires an Affiliated Business Arrangement disclosure. Timing matters because the consumer must receive it before deciding. The ABA disclosure must be provided to the consumer:

answers.text: At or before the time of the referral, with the LE in many cases or no later than the time the referral is made
Only after consummation of the loan
On the day of closing during the signing
Only when the consumer specifically asks for it

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.15 requires the ABA disclosure at or before the time of referral.
explanations.b: Wrong — post-consummation delivery is too late.
explanations.c: Wrong — closing-day delivery defeats the consumer's shopping choice.
explanations.d: Wrong — the disclosure is automatic, not request-based.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: GLBA requires a privacy notice to consumers. Initial timing is governed by Regulation P. The initial privacy notice generally must be provided:

answers.text: Before the consumer makes their initial inquiry by phone or email
No later than the time of establishing a customer relationship, with annual notices when applicable
Only at the consumer's specific written request
Thirty days after consummation, with annual updates thereafter

explanations.a: Wrong — pre-inquiry delivery is not the rule; customer-relationship establishment is the trigger.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1016.4 requires the initial privacy notice no later than when a customer relationship is established.
explanations.c: Wrong — the notice is required automatically, not on request.
explanations.d: Wrong — 30 days post-consummation is past the trigger event.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The Mortgage Servicing Disclosure tells the consumer whether the creditor intends to retain servicing or transfer it. The disclosure is given early in the loan process. The Mortgage Servicing Disclosure Statement must be provided:

answers.text: Within 30 days after consummation of the loan
Only if servicing is actually transferred during the loan term
Within 3 business days after receiving the application
After the borrower's first scheduled payment is due

explanations.a: Wrong — post-consummation delivery does not meet the rule.
explanations.b: Wrong — the disclosure is required regardless of whether transfer occurs.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.33(a) requires the disclosure within 3 business days of application.
explanations.d: Wrong — the disclosure precedes the first payment by months.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The 'Know Before You Owe' framework gives consumers integrated disclosures showing all material credit terms before they commit. Consumer choice depends on clear pricing. Know Before You Owe is implemented through:

answers.text: The TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure rule, including the Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure
The CFPB Credit Card Statement rule for monthly statements
The SAFE Act's licensing requirements for individual MLOs
The HMDA reporting rule for institutions

explanations.a: Correct — the TRID rule under Regulations X and Z implements the Know Before You Owe framework.
explanations.b: Wrong — credit card rules are separate.
explanations.c: Wrong — the SAFE Act addresses licensing, not consumer disclosures.
explanations.d: Wrong — HMDA is data reporting, not consumer disclosure.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: At application, the consumer should receive disclosures explaining their rights, the loan's likely cost, and what to expect at closing. Early disclosures help the consumer evaluate the offer. Which is one of the early disclosures provided after application?

answers.text: The recorded mortgage and note copies post-recording
The final HUD-1 settlement statement at closing
The Loan Estimate showing estimated loan terms and closing costs
The Mortgage Insurance Premium termination notice

explanations.a: Wrong — recorded copies follow closing, not application.
explanations.b: Wrong — the HUD-1 was a closing-time document and has been replaced by the CD.
explanations.c: Correct — the LE is the principal early disclosure under 12 CFR 1026.19(e).
explanations.d: Wrong — MIP termination notices apply later in the loan, not at application.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: When an MLO finds that an LE is missing required information, Regulation Z imposes specific corrective action. The error cannot simply be ignored. If the creditor discovers that an LE delivered to the consumer is incomplete or inaccurate (and a changed circumstance has not occurred), the creditor must:

answers.text: Issue a Closing Disclosure to overwrite the prior Loan Estimate
Skip directly to consummation without further disclosures
Withhold all communication with the consumer until closing
Correct the disclosure as required by Regulation Z, generally by reissuing the LE within 3 business days of receiving information establishing a changed circumstance or correction trigger

explanations.a: Wrong — the CD does not retroactively cure an incomplete LE.
explanations.b: Wrong — proceeding to consummation without correction violates Regulation Z.
explanations.c: Wrong — withholding required disclosures is itself a violation.
explanations.d: Correct — Regulation Z requires correction by issuing a revised disclosure within the regulation's timing rules.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: After receiving the six items required for an application, the creditor's clock for the LE begins to run. Regulation Z imposes both an upper and a lower delivery bound. The initial Loan Estimate must be:

answers.text: Delivered within 24 hours after receipt of the application
Delivered or placed in the mail within 3 business days after application receipt, and at least 7 business days before consummation
Delivered within 7 business days after consummation
Delivered within 10 calendar days after consummation

explanations.a: Wrong — 24 hours is shorter than the regulatory deadline.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(1)(iii) and (e)(1)(iv) require both deadlines.
explanations.c: Wrong — the LE precedes consummation; post-consummation delivery is invalid.
explanations.d: Wrong — the LE is a pre-consummation disclosure.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: A revised LE is permitted only after a defined trigger such as a changed circumstance, a borrower-requested change, or expiration of the LE. Issuing a revised LE without a trigger violates Regulation Z. A creditor may issue a revised LE when:

answers.text: The MLO simply wants to change the price after marketing pressure
The lender's appetite for the loan changes for portfolio reasons
A changed circumstance affects settlement charges, eligibility, or the value of the security property
The consumer is delayed in providing requested documents

explanations.a: Wrong — pricing pressure is not a Regulation Z trigger.
explanations.b: Wrong — portfolio appetite is not a permitted trigger.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(iv) allows revised LEs upon changed circumstances affecting settlement charges, eligibility, or property value.
explanations.d: Wrong — borrower documentation delays alone do not trigger a revised LE.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: After issuing the initial LE, the creditor must keep the disclosed settlement charges available for the consumer to lock in. After this period, the creditor may revise without a triggering event. The LE settlement-charge availability period is:

answers.text: 24 hours from delivery of the LE
5 calendar days from delivery of the LE
7 calendar days from delivery of the LE
10 business days, after which the creditor may revise estimates absent a changed circumstance

explanations.a: Wrong — 24 hours is far shorter than the regulatory minimum.
explanations.b: Wrong — calendar days is the wrong unit; the rule uses business days.
explanations.c: Wrong — 7 calendar days is shorter than the regulatory minimum.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(iv)(E) provides 10 business days of LE availability.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Most CD changes between issuance and closing do not require a new 3-business-day waiting period. A handful of significant changes do trigger a new waiting period. A new 3-day waiting period is required when:

answers.text: The cash to close changes by $50 due to a per-diem recalculation
The APR increases by more than 1/8 of 1 percentage point on a fixed-rate loan, the loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added
A typo in the property address is corrected on the CD
Per-diem interest is recalculated for a one-day closing delay

explanations.a: Wrong — small cash-to-close adjustments do not retrigger the waiting period.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(f)(2)(ii) lists these three changes as the only retrigger conditions.
explanations.c: Wrong — clerical corrections do not retrigger the waiting period.
explanations.d: Wrong — per-diem recalculation alone does not retrigger the waiting period.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Once a consumer indicates intent to proceed, the creditor may charge fees beyond the credit-report fee. The means of expression must be one the LE permitted. A consumer indicates intent to proceed when:

answers.text: The consumer communicates that intent to the creditor by any means specified by the creditor or, in the absence of a specified means, by any reasonable communication
The consumer signs the deed of trust at closing
The MLO confirms intent on the consumer's behalf without consumer action
The consumer's bank wires funds for the down payment

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(2)(i)(A) and Comment 19(e)(2)(i)(A)-2 permit any means specified or, if none, any reasonable communication by the consumer.
explanations.b: Wrong — closing signatures occur much later and define consummation, not intent to proceed.
explanations.c: Wrong — only the consumer can express intent; the MLO cannot do so on the consumer's behalf.
explanations.d: Wrong — wiring funds is a closing-stage act, not intent to proceed.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: If the consumer does not indicate intent to proceed within the LE availability period, the creditor's exposure under the disclosed estimates ends. The creditor may, but need not, reissue a new LE. After the LE settlement-charge availability period expires:

answers.text: The creditor must extend the period for another 10 business days
The CD must be issued immediately to replace the LE
The application is automatically deemed withdrawn
The creditor may revise the estimates and is no longer obligated to honor the original LE charges

explanations.a: Wrong — there is no automatic extension under Regulation Z.
explanations.b: Wrong — the CD is not a substitute for an unaccepted LE.
explanations.c: Wrong — there is no automatic withdrawal upon LE expiration.
explanations.d: Correct — after expiration, the original LE estimates are no longer binding on the creditor.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The CD typically includes a signature line for confirmation of receipt. Whether a signature is required depends on the lender's practice and state law, not on Regulation Z. Under Regulation Z, the consumer's signature on the CD:

answers.text: May be required by the creditor at its option, but is not required by Regulation Z to evidence receipt
Is required by Regulation Z for all loans without exception
Notarizes the loan terms for legal effect
Replaces the Loan Estimate as the operative pricing disclosure

explanations.a: Correct — Regulation Z does not require a signature on the CD; lenders may require it at their option.
explanations.b: Wrong — Regulation Z does not mandate consumer signature on the CD.
explanations.c: Wrong — a signature does not function as a notarization.
explanations.d: Wrong — the LE and CD are separate disclosures with separate functions.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Once a Closing Disclosure is issued, fees cannot be revised upward except for limited reasons. The CD largely locks in the cost picture. After delivery of the CD, the creditor generally:

answers.text: May freely raise lender fees without further disclosure
May add discount points without any further disclosure
May not increase fees absent a changed circumstance, borrower-requested change, or other Regulation Z exception
Must reissue the LE before closing to address pricing changes

explanations.a: Wrong — post-CD increases are restricted to specific exceptions.
explanations.b: Wrong — discount points cannot be added unilaterally without disclosure.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(f) restricts post-CD fee increases to specific Regulation Z exceptions.
explanations.d: Wrong — the LE is not reissued post-CD; the corrected CD is.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: For 1-4 family residential mortgage applications, the lender must give the borrower a list of HUD-approved counselors. The list helps connect borrowers to free or low-cost help. The Homeownership Counseling List must be delivered to the consumer:

answers.text: On the day of consummation alongside the CD
Within 3 business days of receipt of the consumer's mortgage loan application
Within 30 days after consummation
Only if the consumer requests it in writing

explanations.a: Wrong — closing-day delivery is too late.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.20 requires delivery within 3 business days of application.
explanations.c: Wrong — post-consummation delivery does not meet the rule.
explanations.d: Wrong — the delivery is automatic, not request-based.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Loans designated as HOEPA high-cost mortgages require pre-loan counseling. The counseling must be from a HUD-approved counselor and is documented in the loan file. Before a creditor may extend a HOEPA high-cost loan, the borrower must:

answers.text: Receive pre-loan counseling from a HUD-approved counselor or other approved counselor and provide a certification of counseling
Pay a higher loan origination fee than the conforming standard
Sign a written waiver of TILA disclosures and the right of rescission
Confirm in writing that they intend to refinance the loan within 12 months

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.34(a)(5) requires pre-loan counseling from a HUD-approved counselor before consummation of a HOEPA loan.
explanations.b: Wrong — fee surcharges are not the rule.
explanations.c: Wrong — TILA disclosures and rescission rights cannot be waived as a condition of HOEPA loans.
explanations.d: Wrong — refinance commitments are not part of HOEPA's counseling requirement.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: In analyzing assets, the underwriter looks for funds available to close, post-closing reserves, and the seasoning and source of funds. Documentation supports the qualifying decision. Which of the following is generally an acceptable asset for qualifying?

answers.text: Funds owed to the borrower from a personal loan to a relative, undocumented
Funds in the borrower's depository account documented over the agency lookback period
Cash held by the borrower at home, with no paper trail or deposit history
Funds expected to come from a future bonus that has not yet been earned

explanations.a: Wrong — undocumented receivables are not qualifying assets.
explanations.b: Correct — funds in a documented depository account meet agency standards for qualifying assets.
explanations.c: Wrong — cash on hand without a paper trail is generally not allowed by agency standards.
explanations.d: Wrong — anticipated future income is not a current qualifying asset.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Underwriting requires accurate measurement of debt obligations to compute DTI. The credit report and application drive the calculation. Liabilities counted in the DTI calculation typically include:

answers.text: Only the new mortgage payment with no other debt
Only credit card minimum balances
Only secured debts shown on the application
The proposed monthly housing expense plus minimum payments on installment, revolving, and other recurring obligations

explanations.a: Wrong — DTI captures total recurring debt, not the new mortgage alone.
explanations.b: Wrong — installment and other obligations also count.
explanations.c: Wrong — unsecured recurring debts also count toward DTI.
explanations.d: Correct — DTI captures total recurring monthly debt service relative to gross monthly income.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Qualifying income generally includes earnings the borrower can be expected to receive over the loan's foreseeable future. Some income types require additional documentation. Which is generally acceptable as qualifying income?

answers.text: Lottery winnings, unverified by official records
One-time gifts received from a family member
Stable W-2 wages with a 2-year history and continuance reasonably expected
Gambling proceeds reported informally to the lender

explanations.a: Wrong — unverified one-time receipts are not qualifying.
explanations.b: Wrong — one-time gifts are not recurring income.
explanations.c: Correct — stable wages with documented history and likely continuance are core qualifying income.
explanations.d: Wrong — informal gambling proceeds do not qualify.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Self-employed borrowers' income is verified through tax returns and supporting documentation. Underwriting often requires multiple years of returns. Self-employed borrowers typically must provide:

answers.text: Their employer's most recent paystub for each month of the year
Two years of personal and business tax returns, with year-to-date profit and loss as required by the agency
A signed affidavit from a personal friend describing the business
Only the most recent credit report, with no income documentation

explanations.a: Wrong — self-employed borrowers do not have an employer paystub.
explanations.b: Correct — agency standards require two years of returns and a YTD P&L for self-employed income.
explanations.c: Wrong — affidavits do not substitute for returns.
explanations.d: Wrong — credit reports do not document income.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Rental income from a borrower-owned investment property may count toward qualifying with documentation. Lenders generally apply a vacancy/expense factor. Rental income on a non-owner-occupied investment property is typically:

answers.text: Counted at 100% of gross rent
Counted at 100% of net rent without supporting documentation
Excluded entirely if the property carries a mortgage
Counted at 75% of gross rent (less the property's PITIA), reflecting a 25% vacancy/expense factor or as the agency standard provides

explanations.a: Wrong — 100% of gross overstates net rental income.
explanations.b: Wrong — net rent claims still require documentation.
explanations.c: Wrong — having a mortgage does not exclude rental income.
explanations.d: Correct — agency rules typically apply a 75% factor to gross rents to recognize vacancy and expenses.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The credit report informs underwriting on debts, payment history, public records, and inquiries. The credit report is also tied to disclosure rules. After a credit pull, an MLO may:

answers.text: Use the report to evaluate creditworthiness, while complying with FCRA's adverse-action and risk-based-pricing rules when applicable
Sell the report to other lenders for marketing purposes
Disregard the report entirely if it contains adverse information
Pull a credit report on the borrower's children for added context

explanations.a: Correct — FCRA permits use for permissible-purpose underwriting and triggers consumer notices when applicable.
explanations.b: Wrong — selling the report violates FCRA.
explanations.c: Wrong — disregarding adverse information would also be improper.
explanations.d: Wrong — reports on minors not party to the transaction lack permissible purpose.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Underwriting evaluates whether income is stable and likely to continue. Declining trends may require additional analysis or exclusion. When evaluating an income trend, the underwriter:

answers.text: Counts the highest year's earnings only and ignores other years
Discards the most recent year if it is the lowest of the period
Considers stability and the likelihood of continuance, often using the lower or average figure when income is declining
Doubles the most recent month's pay for an annual projection

explanations.a: Wrong — cherry-picking the highest year overstates likely continuance.
explanations.b: Wrong — discarding the most recent year ignores the trend.
explanations.c: Correct — agency standards take a conservative view of declining income trends.
explanations.d: Wrong — annualizing one month's pay is not standard underwriting.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: LTV measures the loan amount against the property value. It is a foundational underwriting metric. LTV is computed as:

answers.text: The total monthly debt divided by gross monthly income
The annual interest divided by the principal balance
The loan amount divided by the lesser of the property's appraised value or sales price (for a purchase)
The borrower's net worth divided by the loan amount sought

explanations.a: Wrong — that formula is DTI, not LTV.
explanations.b: Wrong — that ratio is an interest-rate-style figure, not LTV.
explanations.c: Correct — agency rules define LTV as loan amount over the lesser of value or sales price for purchases.
explanations.d: Wrong — net worth is not part of LTV.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: DTI measures the borrower's debts against their income. The figure helps assess capacity to repay. DTI is computed as:

answers.text: Total monthly recurring debt obligations (including the new housing payment) divided by gross monthly income
The loan amount divided by the appraised property value
The borrower's net assets divided by their gross income
The credit-card minimum payments divided by net monthly income

explanations.a: Correct — back-end DTI captures total monthly debt service over gross monthly income.
explanations.b: Wrong — that ratio is LTV, not DTI.
explanations.c: Wrong — net assets are not part of DTI.
explanations.d: Wrong — DTI uses gross income and includes all recurring debt, not just credit-card minimums.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Regulation Z's Ability-to-Repay rule requires creditors to make a reasonable, good-faith determination that the consumer can repay. The rule lists factors that must be considered. Under the ATR rule, the creditor must consider, at a minimum:

answers.text: The borrower's social media activity and online presence

Eight underwriting factors including current/expected income or assets, employment status, the monthly mortgage payment, monthly payments on simultaneous loans, monthly payments for mortgage-related obligations, current debt obligations, monthly DTI or residual income, and credit history
Only the borrower's credit score from one bureau
Only the property's appraised value as collateral

explanations.a: Wrong — social media activity is not part of ATR.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.43(c)(2) lists these eight ATR factors.
explanations.c: Wrong — credit score alone is not the ATR test.
explanations.d: Wrong — ATR is repayment-capacity, not collateral-only.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: A Qualified Mortgage receives heightened protection under the ATR rule. QMs limit certain risky product features and cap points and fees. A QM generally:

answers.text: May have negative amortization throughout the term
May include interest-only periods of any length
May exceed a 40-year amortization term
Limits points and fees, prohibits negative amortization, interest-only payments, and balloons (with limited exceptions), and caps the loan term at 30 years

explanations.a: Wrong — negative amortization is excluded from QMs.
explanations.b: Wrong — interest-only periods are excluded from QMs.
explanations.c: Wrong — terms over 30 years are excluded from QMs.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.43(e) sets these QM constraints.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: When a property has more than one lien, lenders look at the combined position. Combined LTV captures total leverage. CLTV is computed as:

answers.text: The first-mortgage balance only divided by the sales price
The down payment divided by the purchase price
Insurance premiums divided by the appraised value
The total of all liens secured by the property divided by the lesser of the appraised value or sales price

explanations.a: Wrong — first-mortgage-only is LTV, not CLTV.
explanations.b: Wrong — that fraction is a down-payment ratio.
explanations.c: Wrong — insurance premiums are not part of CLTV.
explanations.d: Correct — CLTV includes all secured liens against the property's value or price.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: An appraisal supplies an independent value opinion to support the loan decision. Lenders rely on it for collateral risk. The primary purpose of a residential appraisal is to:

answers.text: Determine the borrower's credit score and credit history
Set the property tax assessment for the local taxing authority
Provide an opinion of the property's market value as of an effective date
Calculate the borrower's debt-to-income ratio

explanations.a: Wrong — credit scoring is unrelated to appraisal.
explanations.b: Wrong — tax assessments are made by local assessors, not appraisers for mortgage purposes.
explanations.c: Correct — appraisals develop a market-value opinion as of an effective date.
explanations.d: Wrong — DTI calculation does not depend on appraisals.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Appraisers use multiple methods to develop an opinion of value. Selection depends on property type and data availability. The three traditional appraisal approaches are:

answers.text: The sales comparison, cost, and income approaches
The capital gains, principal payment, and yield approaches
The loan-to-value, debt-to-income, and combined-loan-to-value approaches
The discounted cash flow, gross rent multiplier, and bond-yield approaches

explanations.a: Correct — these are the three traditional approaches recognized in residential appraisal.
explanations.b: Wrong — those are not appraisal approaches.
explanations.c: Wrong — those are underwriting ratios, not appraisal methods.
explanations.d: Wrong — those are securities/finance methods, not appraisal approaches.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: For most owner-occupied 1-4 family residential properties, one approach is given the most weight. Comparable sales drive the value conclusion. The primary approach for typical owner-occupied 1-4 family residential properties is generally:

answers.text: The cost approach, based on replacement cost
The sales comparison approach, using recent comparable sales
The discounted cash flow approach used for commercial real estate
The gross rent multiplier approach used for rental analysis

explanations.a: Wrong — the cost approach is supportive but not primary for typical residential.
explanations.b: Correct — sales comparison is the primary approach for typical residential properties.
explanations.c: Wrong — DCF is a commercial approach, not standard residential.
explanations.d: Wrong — GRM applies to rentals, not typical owner-occupied homes.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: To prevent improper influence on appraisers, Regulation Z and agency rules establish independence standards. The rules separate sales/loan production from appraisal selection. Regulation Z's appraisal independence rule:

answers.text: Prohibits any person with an interest in the transaction from coercing, influencing, or attempting to influence an appraiser to misstate the property's value
Allows lenders to share their internal target value with the appraiser before assignment
Requires the borrower to select the appraiser personally
Bans all communication between the lender and the appraiser at all times

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.42(c) bans coercion or improper influence on appraisers.
explanations.b: Wrong — sharing target values is the kind of coercion the rule prohibits.
explanations.c: Wrong — borrowers do not pick appraisers under Regulation Z.
explanations.d: Wrong — proper communication is permitted; only improper influence is banned.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: For HPMLs, Regulation Z imposes appraisal protections. The protections include a written appraisal and a physical interior visit. An HPML appraisal must be performed by a:

answers.text: Licensed real estate broker familiar with the area
Mortgage broker with local market knowledge
Certified home inspector with appraisal training
Certified or licensed appraiser, with a physical interior visit and a written appraisal report

explanations.a: Wrong — real-estate brokers are not appraisers.
explanations.b: Wrong — mortgage brokers are not appraisers.
explanations.c: Wrong — home inspectors are not appraisers.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.35(c) requires a certified or licensed appraiser, an interior visit, and a written report on HPMLs.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: ECOA's appraisal-copy rule requires the creditor to deliver the appraisal to the borrower on first-lien residential mortgage applications. Delivery must occur regardless of whether the loan closes. The creditor must provide the appraisal copy to the consumer:

answers.text: Only at consummation alongside the CD
Only if the appraisal value is below the contract price
Promptly upon completion or no later than 3 business days before consummation, whichever is earlier
Only if the consumer pays an additional fee for delivery

explanations.a: Wrong — closing-time delivery does not meet the rule.
explanations.b: Wrong — value below contract is not the trigger; copies are required regardless.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.14(a)(1) sets the 'promptly upon completion or 3 business days before consummation, whichever is earlier' deadline.
explanations.d: Wrong — delivery is provided without additional fee.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Before closing, the title agent issues a preliminary title report or commitment. The document discloses defects, liens, and exceptions to title. A preliminary title report typically:

answers.text: Guarantees clear title to the property forever
Identifies the current vesting, liens, encumbrances, and exceptions to title that the title insurer will not cover
Replaces the deed for purposes of conveyance
Functions as the lender's payoff statement on a refinance

explanations.a: Wrong — no title document guarantees title forever; insurance covers identified risks.
explanations.b: Correct — preliminary title reports identify vesting, liens, exceptions, and conditions before issuing a final policy.
explanations.c: Wrong — the deed conveys title; the title report does not.
explanations.d: Wrong — payoff statements come from the existing creditor, not from title.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Title insurance protects against losses from title defects discovered after closing. Two policy types serve different beneficiaries. The lender's title insurance policy:

answers.text: Protects the seller against future buyer claims after closing
Protects only the appraiser from valuation challenges
Protects the lender's lien position up to the loan amount and decreases as the loan is paid down
Replaces the owner's title insurance policy entirely

explanations.a: Wrong — title policies for the lender do not protect the seller.
explanations.b: Wrong — appraisers are not parties to title policies.
explanations.c: Correct — the lender's policy protects the lender's lien up to the loan balance.
explanations.d: Wrong — owner's and lender's policies are separate.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Owner's title insurance is optional in most states but commonly recommended. It runs to the property owner and lasts as long as the owner has an interest. An owner's title insurance policy:

answers.text: Is required by Regulation Z on all loans without exception
Protects the owner against loss from covered title defects existing as of the policy date
Protects only the lender's lien up to the loan amount
Eliminates the need for a property survey

explanations.a: Wrong — Regulation Z does not require owner's policies.
explanations.b: Correct — the owner's policy protects against covered defects existing at the policy's effective date.
explanations.c: Wrong — that description fits the lender's policy, not the owner's.
explanations.d: Wrong — owner's policies do not eliminate survey requirements.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Title work begins shortly after the application and continues through closing. The chronology supports the lender's lien priority. Which of the following is the typical sequence?

answers.text: Title insurance issued, then preliminary title report ordered, then deed search done last
Closing completed, title commitment ordered, application taken, deed search done
Application taken, closing completed, then title commitment ordered, then recording
Application taken, title order and search, preliminary commitment, clearing exceptions, recording, then final policy issued

explanations.a: Wrong — preliminary work comes before final policy issuance.
explanations.b: Wrong — title work precedes closing, not the reverse.
explanations.c: Wrong — title commitment is ordered before closing.
explanations.d: Correct — title work is ordered shortly after application, with the final policy issued after recording.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Hazard insurance protects the property from physical loss from covered perils. The lender requires it because the property secures the loan. Hazard insurance on a residential mortgage typically:

answers.text: Is required by the lender at coverage at least equal to the lesser of replacement cost or the loan balance, with the lender named as mortgagee/loss payee
Is paid only at consummation as a one-time premium for the loan term
Is optional after the first year of the loan
Is provided by the lender to the borrower at no cost as a marketing benefit

explanations.a: Correct — lender insurance requirements track loan balance/replacement cost and require mortgagee endorsement.
explanations.b: Wrong — premiums are typically paid annually or via escrow.
explanations.c: Wrong — hazard insurance is required throughout the loan, not only the first year.
explanations.d: Wrong — hazard insurance is purchased by the borrower, not provided by the lender.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: For properties in a Special Flood Hazard Area, federal law requires flood insurance on federally related mortgages. The requirement is mandatory for the life of the loan. Flood insurance through the National Flood Insurance Program is required when:

answers.text: The property is anywhere in the United States
The borrower's credit score is below 680
The loan amount exceeds $250,000
The property securing a federally related mortgage is located in a Special Flood Hazard Area as designated by FEMA

explanations.a: Wrong — flood insurance is not required everywhere.
explanations.b: Wrong — credit score is irrelevant to flood-zone designation.
explanations.c: Wrong — loan size is not the trigger.
explanations.d: Correct — 42 USC 4012a requires flood insurance on federally related loans secured by property in an SFHA.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: On conventional loans with less than 20% down, lenders typically require private mortgage insurance. PMI protects the lender from default loss. Borrower-paid PMI is generally required when the LTV exceeds:

answers.text: 80% on a conventional loan, until the LTV reaches the HPA cancellation thresholds
50% on any loan
95% on FHA-insured loans
100% LTV regardless of program

explanations.a: Correct — PMI is typically required on conventional loans above 80% LTV.
explanations.b: Wrong — 50% is far below typical PMI requirement thresholds.
explanations.c: Wrong — FHA loans use MIP, not PMI, and the threshold is different.
explanations.d: Wrong — 100% LTV is not a typical PMI threshold.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: FHA loans use mortgage insurance to protect the FHA insurance fund. The premium has both upfront and annual components. FHA mortgage insurance:

answers.text: Cancels at 80% LTV upon borrower request, like conventional PMI
Includes an upfront MIP and an annual MIP, with cancellation rules that depend on the LTV at origination and the loan term
Is optional for the borrower on FHA loans
Is identical to PMI on conventional loans in all respects

explanations.a: Wrong — FHA MIP cancellation does not follow HPA's borrower-request rule for PMI.
explanations.b: Correct — FHA MIP has UFMIP plus annual MIP, with cancellation per FHA program rules tied to LTV and term.
explanations.c: Wrong — MIP is required on FHA loans.
explanations.d: Wrong — FHA MIP differs structurally and contractually from conventional PMI.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: VA loans require a one-time funding fee that supports the VA loan guaranty program. The fee may be financed into the loan. The VA funding fee:

answers.text: Replaces the borrower's hazard insurance premium
Is paid monthly to the VA over the life of the loan
Is a one-time fee charged on most VA loans, with amount based on loan type, down payment, and prior VA loan use, that may be financed
Cancels automatically at 80% LTV based on original value

explanations.a: Wrong — the funding fee is not a hazard insurance substitute.
explanations.b: Wrong — the fee is a one-time charge, not monthly.
explanations.c: Correct — VA funding fee structure varies by loan type, down payment, and prior VA use; financing is permitted.
explanations.d: Wrong — VA loans do not have automatic LTV-based fee cancellation.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: USDA Rural Development guaranteed loans use fees instead of PMI. The fees support the USDA program. USDA guaranteed loans use:

answers.text: PMI cancellable at 80% LTV based on original value
An upfront guarantee fee plus an annual fee, both of which may generally be financed in part
FHA MIP under FHA program rules
The VA funding fee structure for veteran borrowers

explanations.a: Wrong — USDA does not use conventional PMI.
explanations.b: Correct — USDA guaranteed loans use upfront and annual fees, with financing options.
explanations.c: Wrong — FHA MIP applies to FHA-insured loans only.
explanations.d: Wrong — VA funding fee applies to VA loans only.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: At closing, a neutral party coordinates document signing and disbursement of funds. The agent's role differs by state. The settlement (closing) agent generally:

answers.text: Conducts the closing, oversees document execution, and disburses funds in accordance with the lender's closing instructions
Underwrites the loan and issues the credit decision
Sets the interest rate on the loan
Issues the appraisal report on the property

explanations.a: Correct — settlement agents conduct closing per the lender's instructions.
explanations.b: Wrong — underwriting is performed by the lender, not the settlement agent.
explanations.c: Wrong — interest rate is set by the lender's pricing.
explanations.d: Wrong — appraisals are issued by appraisers, not settlement agents.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: A power of attorney allows another person to sign on a borrower's behalf at closing. Lender approval is required and additional formalities apply. A power of attorney for a mortgage closing must generally:

answers.text: Be an oral authorization made on the day of closing
Be granted to a party unrelated to the transaction
Be in writing, properly executed (and recorded as required by state law), lender-approved, and current at closing
Be granted to the MLO who originated the loan

explanations.a: Wrong — oral POAs are insufficient for mortgage closings.
explanations.b: Wrong — relationship requirements vary; the rule is execution and approval, not unrelated status.
explanations.c: Correct — written, properly executed, lender-approved, current POAs are typical requirements.
explanations.d: Wrong — granting a POA to the originating MLO creates conflicts and is generally prohibited.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: At closing, several core documents transfer interests, evidence the debt, secure the lender, and disclose terms. The package varies by state but the core is consistent. Core residential mortgage closing documents include:

answers.text: A SAR filing and a Form 4506-C as the primary closing documents
A privacy notice and an appraisal copy as the primary closing documents
The credit report, appraisal, and property survey as the binding closing documents
The promissory note, the security instrument (mortgage or deed of trust), the Closing Disclosure, and the deed (in a purchase)

explanations.a: Wrong — these are file documents, not the core closing instruments.
explanations.b: Wrong — these are disclosures, not closing instruments.
explanations.c: Wrong — these are due-diligence documents, not the binding closing package.
explanations.d: Correct — these are the principal closing documents in a residential mortgage transaction.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: All parties needed to convey title or assume liability must sign at closing. State law dictates many of the rules. Which of the following typically signs the security instrument?

answers.text: All parties holding a title interest in the property, including non-borrowing spouses where required by state homestead or community-property law
Only the lender's representative at closing
The settlement agent only, as a neutral party
The real estate agent representing the buyer or seller

explanations.a: Correct — title-holders sign the security instrument; spousal signatures are added where state law requires.
explanations.b: Wrong — the lender's representative signs lender documents but not the security instrument as the grantor.
explanations.c: Wrong — the settlement agent does not grant the security interest.
explanations.d: Wrong — real estate agents do not sign the security instrument.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: States divide between 'wet' and 'dry' funding rules. The distinction governs when funds disburse relative to closing. In a 'wet' funding state:

answers.text: Funding is delayed until after rescission expires on a purchase loan
Funding is delayed until 30 days after the closing date
Funds disburse at or shortly after closing, generally on the same day documents are signed
Funds never disburse until after public recording of the mortgage

explanations.a: Wrong — purchases are not subject to rescission.
explanations.b: Wrong — 30-day delay is not the wet-funding norm.
explanations.c: Correct — wet states disburse funds at or near closing on the day of signing.
explanations.d: Wrong — wet funding does not require recording before disbursement.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: On loans subject to the right of rescission, funds may not disburse until the rescission period expires. The rule preserves the consumer's cancellation right. On a refinance with a new creditor secured by the principal dwelling, funding is delayed until:

answers.text: The CD is signed by the consumer
The 3-business-day rescission period has expired without rescission
The deed and mortgage are recorded in the public record
The consumer pays the appraisal fee in full

explanations.a: Wrong — CD signing alone does not unlock funding for rescindable loans.
explanations.b: Correct — Regulation Z prohibits disbursement until the rescission period expires.
explanations.c: Wrong — recording does not control rescission-related funding delay.
explanations.d: Wrong — appraisal payment does not control rescission timing.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: At closing, the consumer reviews fees on the CD. Some fees are loan-related, some are property-related, some are prepaids. Which of the following typically appears in the prepaids section of the CD?

answers.text: Lender origination charges paid at closing
Title insurance premiums paid at closing
Recording fees paid to the county recorder
Per-diem prepaid interest, the initial premium for hazard insurance, and any property tax prepaid at closing

explanations.a: Wrong — origination charges are loan costs, not prepaids.
explanations.b: Wrong — title insurance is in services, not prepaids.
explanations.c: Wrong — recording fees are taxes/other government charges, not prepaids.
explanations.d: Correct — prepaids cover charges paid in advance for the borrower's account, such as per-diem interest, initial hazard premium, and prepaid taxes.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Periodic interest accrues on the unpaid principal each period. Most residential mortgages use a monthly accrual. Periodic interest on a fixed-rate residential mortgage is typically computed as:

answers.text: Daily simple interest based on a 360-day year only
The annual interest rate divided by 360, applied to the original loan amount each month
The annual interest rate divided by 12, applied to the unpaid principal balance to produce the monthly interest portion of the payment
The annual rate multiplied by the loan amount with no division by months

explanations.a: Wrong — daily simple interest applies to a different product class, not standard fixed monthly accrual.
explanations.b: Wrong — applying to the original loan amount each month would produce constant interest, not amortizing interest.
explanations.c: Correct — monthly interest on a fixed-rate amortizing loan = (annual rate / 12) × unpaid principal.
explanations.d: Wrong — that yields one year's interest, not a periodic accrual.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The monthly P&I payment on a fully amortizing fixed-rate loan is computed using the loan amount, rate, and term. Online calculators apply the standard formula. The monthly principal-and-interest payment on a fully amortizing fixed-rate loan is:

answers.text: Calculated by simply dividing the loan amount by the term in months
The interest portion only, with principal paid at maturity
The interest portion plus a flat principal of 1% of the original loan amount each month
Calculated using the standard amortization formula based on loan amount, periodic interest rate, and number of periodic payments

explanations.a: Wrong — that ignores interest entirely.
explanations.b: Wrong — that describes interest-only loans, not fully amortizing.
explanations.c: Wrong — flat 1% principal does not match standard amortization.
explanations.d: Correct — fully amortizing P&I uses the standard amortization formula.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: The down payment is the portion of the purchase price paid by the borrower at closing. It funds the equity that drives LTV. The down payment is:

answers.text: The difference between the contract sales price and the loan amount, paid by the borrower in eligible funds at closing
The borrower's first monthly mortgage payment
The seller's contribution to the buyer's closing costs
The lender's origination fee on the loan

explanations.a: Correct — down payment = sales price minus loan amount, paid by the borrower.
explanations.b: Wrong — first payment occurs after closing.
explanations.c: Wrong — seller credits are not down payment funds.
explanations.d: Wrong — origination fees are loan costs, not down payment.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: Closing costs include third-party fees and lender charges. Prepaids cover items paid in advance for the borrower's account. Prepaids typically include:

answers.text: Origination fees and underwriting fees paid at closing
Per-diem interest, the initial homeowner's insurance premium, and the initial escrow deposit for property taxes and insurance
Recording fees and transfer taxes
Owner's title insurance premium and lender's title policy premium paid at the closing table

explanations.a: Wrong — origination and underwriting are loan costs.
explanations.b: Correct — prepaids consist of items paid in advance for the borrower's account.
explanations.c: Wrong — recording and transfer taxes are government charges, not prepaids.
explanations.d: Wrong — title insurance is in the services category.

questions.name: Mortgage Loan Origination Activities
questions.text: On an ARM, after the initial fixed period, the rate adjusts according to the index, margin, and caps. Caps limit the magnitude of changes. After the initial fixed period on a typical ARM, the new interest rate is generally calculated as:

answers.text: Whatever the lender chooses in its discretion
The index minus the margin, subject to lifetime cap only
The margin minus the index, with no cap
The current index plus the margin, subject to periodic and lifetime rate caps

explanations.a: Wrong — discretion would defeat the predictable formula promised in disclosures.
explanations.b: Wrong — the formula adds the margin; subtracting it would understate.
explanations.c: Wrong — that inverts the formula.
explanations.d: Correct — fully indexed ARM rate = index + margin, subject to caps.
